description: Verify that DUT retransmits DHCPDISCOVER with doubling backoff capped at an upper bound (RFC 2131 §4.1 MUST)
approach:
[Objective]
RFC 2131 §4.1 mandates exponential backoff for DISCOVER retransmissions: each retx interval doubles, capped at an upper bound (typically 64 s; the harness uses a fast-envelope cap for test speed). This prevents the client from polling forever at a fixed rate.

[Scenario — chronological]
1. Tester silent: server emul does NOT respond to any DISCOVER.
2. DUT → wire: DISCOVER #1 → DISCOVER #2 → ... → DISCOVER #6
   • interval(k+1, k) doubles each time, capped at fast-envelope upper bound   ← key check

[Pass condition]
All 6 DISCOVERs observed AND each consecutive interval is the prior interval × 2 (or capped at the bound).

[Fail condition]
• Fail_no_discover_<k> — DISCOVER #k missing
• Fail_cap_exceeded — DUT's retx interval exceeds the cap

verdicts.Pass: DUT followed doubling backoff with cap — normal
verdicts.Fail_no_discover: No DUT DHCPDISCOVER within the listen window
verdicts.Fail_cap_exceeded: DUT retx interval exceeds the cap
